facts.text: Forward Collision Warning (FCW) is a car and truck function that warns the driver of an imminent crash ahead but leaves braking to the driver.
facts.quote: Forward Collision Warning (FCW) is the car and truck function that warns the driver of an imminent crash ahead but leaves the braking to the driver.

facts.text: The booklet uses Forward Collision Warning (FCW) research to understand how people respond to imperfect warnings, treating FCW as the road counterpart of the manufacturer's existing proximity warning.
facts.quote: It is the road cousin of the manufacturer's existing proximity warning, and the booklet uses FCW research for what it shows about how people respond to imperfect warnings.

facts.text: On-road Forward Collision Warning (FCW) evidence linked an 18% false alarm rate to truck drivers ignoring FCW (12%) or giving up on FCW (11%).
facts.quote: An 18% false alarm rate was linked to truck drivers ignoring FCW (12%) or giving up on it (11%) [Chapter 4].

facts.text: In road-vehicle simulators, Forward Collision Warning warnings with 20 to 33% false alarms still shortened brake reactions.
facts.quote: Yet in simulators, warnings with 20 to 33% false alarms still shortened brake reactions

facts.text: A 2025 on-road Forward Collision Warning study found no "cry wolf" effect at 33% false alarms, although the warnings caused unnecessary braking.
facts.quote: a 2025 study found no "cry wolf" effect at 33% false alarms, though it caused unnecessary braking [Chapter 4].

facts.text: In real road driving, Forward Collision Warning false alerts were 12% when turning versus 2% during lane keeping.
facts.quote: In real driving, false alerts were 12% when turning against 2% in lane keeping

facts.text: In real road driving, drivers turned Forward Collision Warning sensitivity down over time.
facts.quote: drivers turned sensitivity down over time [Chapter 4].

facts.text: On-road Forward Collision Warning research found that unnecessary alarms with a visible cause hurt trust less than alarms with no visible cause.
facts.quote: Unnecessary alarms with a visible cause hurt trust less than alarms with no visible cause [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Forward Collision Warning research provides the best available evidence on how false alarm rates affect whether warnings are heeded, but that evidence comes from drivers on highways rather than off-road machine operators.
facts.quote: FCW research is the best available evidence on how false alarm rates affect whether warnings are heeded, but it comes from drivers on highways.

facts.text: An accepted false alarm rate for off-road machines was not found.
facts.quote: An accepted false alarm rate for off-road machines was not found [Chapter 4].
